title: The Elijah Cycle
hint: The prophet who challenged Baal (1 Kings 17-19)
intro: Elijah is one of the most dramatic prophets in the Old Testament. In three chapters, he challenges King Ahab and the worship of Baal, experiences God's care in the wilderness, and meets God on Mount Horeb. These chapters display God's power over nature and idols.

items.title: Elijah Proclaims Drought
items.text: Elijah from Tishbe said to Ahab: 'As surely as the Lord lives... there will be no dew or rain in these years except by my word.' (17:1)

items.title: Ravens Feed Elijah
items.text: At the brook Cherith, Elijah was fed by ravers - bread and meat morning and evening. He drank from the brook. (17:2-7)

items.title: The Widow of Zarephath
items.text: The widow had only a handful of flour and a little oil. But the flour did not run out and the oil did not dry up, according to the word of the Lord through Elijah. (17:8-16)

items.title: The Widow's Son Raised
items.text: The boy died, but Elijah lay on him three times and cried out to the Lord. The boy came back to life. (17:17-24)

items.title: The Confrontation on Mount Carmel
items.text: Elijah challenged the 450 prophets of Baal: 'The god who answers by fire, he is God.' Fire fell from heaven and consumed Elijah's offering. The people fell down: 'The Lord, he is God!' (18:20-40)

items.title: The Rain Comes
items.text: After three and a half years, Elijah prayed for rain. A cloud as small as a man's hand rose from the sea, and the sky became black with clouds. (18:41-46)

items.title: Flight to Horeb
items.text: Jezebel threatened Elijah's life. He fled to the wilderness and asked to die. An angel provided him with food, and he traveled forty days to Horeb. (19:1-8)

items.title: God Speaks in the Whisper
items.text: On Horeb there came a great wind, an earthquake and fire - but the Lord was not in them. Then came a still, small whisper. There God spoke to Elijah. (19:9-18)

footer.title: Elijah in the New Testament
footer.content: Jesus is compared with Elijah, and John the Baptist came 'in the spirit and power of Elijah' (Luke 1:17). Elijah met Jesus on the Mount of Transfiguration (Matthew 17). The letter of James uses Elijah's prayer as an example of the power of faith (James 5:17-18).
